verdict.headline: High-risk agreement containing severe non-compete clauses, US jurisdiction, and heavy liquidated damages inside an NDA.
summary: The agreement includes an aggressive non-compete and customer non-solicitation clause that restrains your existing business across ASEAN.
It imposes an uncapped liquidated damages fee of USD 250,000 per violation plus mandatory legal fees under New York courts.
The confidentiality protections are entirely one-sided in favour of the vendor.

findings.title: Extensive 3-year non-compete restriction
findings.quote: Accordingly, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years thereafter, the Counterparty shall not, and shall procure that its affiliates, directors and shareholders shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, develop, market or invest in any business that competes with any business of the Group anywhere in the Territory, including the design or sale of irrigation controllers, soil sensors or farm analytics software.
findings.why_risky: An NDA should only protect shared secrets, not restrict your right to operate in the market. This clause shuts down your ability to sell or develop your own core agritech products across all ASEAN countries for up to six years.
findings.standard: A standard NDA contains no non-compete restrictions, and expressly confirms that the recipient remains free to develop and sell competing solutions independently.
findings.suggested_ask: Please remove Section 6 entirely; non-compete restrictions do not belong in a preliminary confidentiality agreement.

citations.title: Non-compete inside an NDA
citations.excerpt: - **A standard NDA has no non-compete at all.** It protects information, not market position. - Many standard forms say the opposite: the receiver remains free to build or buy similar products, as long as it does not misuse the confidential information. - Where a business restriction is genuinely needed (for example in an exclusive distribution deal), it belongs in the main commercial agreement...

findings.title: Broad non-solicitation and customer non-deal restriction
findings.quote: During the same period, the Counterparty shall not solicit, or accept business from, any person that was a customer or distributor of the Group in the Territory at any time during the term of this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: This stops you from even accepting unsolicited business from any past or present customer or distributor of Halvexa across Southeast Asia, which functions as an indirect trade restraint.
findings.standard: Non-solicitation clauses in NDAs are typically limited to key employees directly involved in discussions for 6 to 12 months, rather than broad bans on customers or business partners.
findings.suggested_ask: Please remove Section 6.3, or limit non-solicitation strictly to key personnel involved in our discussions.

citations.title: Non-solicitation of staff (NDA)
citations.excerpt: - **Mutual**: both sides make the same promise. - **Short**: 6 to 12 months after the NDA ends. - **Narrow**: covers only employees the other side actually met or worked with during the discussions. - **Carve-out for general hiring**: job adverts and recruiters not aimed at the other side's staff do not count, and neither does hiring someone who applies on their own initiative.

findings.title: Severe liquidated damages per breach
findings.quote: In addition to any other remedy, the Counterparty shall pay to Halvexa, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, the sum of USD 250,000 for each breach of this Agreement, without any limit on the aggregate amount payable, together with all attorneys' fees and costs incurred by Halvexa in enforcing this Agreement.
findings.why_risky: Setting a fixed pre-agreed sum of USD 250,000 for every single breach without an overall cap creates an immense financial exposure for minor or technical infractions.
findings.standard: Standard NDAs rely on ordinary legal damages proven in court and injunctions, without pre-set liquidated damages penalties.
findings.suggested_ask: Please delete Section 8.2 and Section 8.3 so that damages are based on actual, proven losses.

citations.title: Liability and remedies, including fixed damages (NDA)
citations.excerpt: - **Ordinary remedies**: the injured side can claim the loss it can actually prove. - **Injunction**: both sides accept that a court may order a stop to a breach quickly, because money may not fix leaked secrets. This is standard and fair. - **No fixed damages sum.** Most standard NDAs do not set a pre-agreed amount payable per breach. - **The same rules for both sides.** - Often no cap on liab...

findings.title: Distant governing law and exclusive New York jurisdiction
findings.quote: Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, and waives any objection to venue in such courts, including any objection that such courts are an inconvenient forum.
findings.why_risky: Defending against any claim in New York courts would involve prohibitive legal expenses, hiring US attorneys, and high travel costs for a Malaysian company.
findings.standard: For contracts involving Southeast Asian business discussions, dispute resolution should take place locally in Malaysia or neutral Singapore.
findings.suggested_ask: Please change the governing law to Malaysian or Singapore law, with dispute resolution or arbitration locally in Kuala Lumpur or Singapore.

citations.title: Governing law: which country's law applies (NDA)
citations.excerpt: - For two Malaysian companies: **Malaysian law**, courts in Malaysia (often Kuala Lumpur). - For a Malaysian and a Singaporean company: **Malaysian or Singapore law**, with the matching courts. Both are common, familiar and close to home. - Either side may still seek an urgent injunction in any court where the other side is. - Non-exclusive jurisdiction is friendlier than exclusive jurisdiction...

findings.title: One-sided assignment rights
findings.quote: Halvexa may assign this Agreement to any member of the Group without the Counterparty's consent. The Counterparty shall not assign this Agreement without Halvexa's prior written consent.
findings.why_risky: The vendor can transfer this agreement to any affiliate without your consent, while you are barred from transferring your rights even during a corporate restructuring.
findings.standard: Assignment rules should be mutual, requiring mutual consent except in routine mergers or acquisitions.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the assignment provision mutual so neither party may assign without the other's prior written consent.

citations.title: Assignment: passing the contract to someone else (NDA)
citations.excerpt: - **Neither side** may assign without the other's written consent. - **Exception:** either side may assign to a company that takes over all or most of its business in a merger or sale, without needing consent. - Consent is not to be unreasonably withheld.

missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please make the confidentiality obligations mutual so that any information Lumio Tani discloses is equally protected.

verdict.headline: High-risk contract: the vendor owns your custom app, caps its liability to one month of fees, and takes an unrestricted indemnity.
summary: The vendor retains all intellectual property in your custom app, refuses to hand over source code, and can remove the app upon termination.
Liability terms are severely unbalanced: the vendor's liability is capped at just one month of fees while your liability is completely uncapped.
You are required to indemnify the vendor for any losses even if caused by the vendor's own negligence, with zero reverse indemnity for IP infringement.

findings.title: Vendor retains ownership and source code of custom software
findings.quote: All Intellectual Property Rights in the Deliverables, including any software developed specifically for the Customer, shall vest in and remain with the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: You are paying for custom software development, but you will only receive a temporary licence that ends upon contract termination. You cannot take your app to another developer or keep operating it if you leave this vendor.
findings.standard: Custom deliverables developed specifically for the customer should transfer to the customer upon full payment of development fees, alongside source code delivery or escrow.
findings.suggested_ask: Can we amend Clause 5.2 so that all intellectual property rights in custom deliverables and the bespoke source code transfer to us upon payment of the development fees?

findings.title: Unilateral limitation of liability favoring vendor only
findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement limits the Customer's liability to the Vendor, and the limitations in Clauses 7.1 and 7.2 apply to the Vendor only.
findings.why_risky: Your company faces unlimited liability for any breach or indirect loss, whereas the vendor enjoys strong exclusions and an extremely low cap.
findings.standard: Limitations of liability and exclusions of consequential loss should be mutual, protecting both parties equally.
findings.suggested_ask: Can Clauses 7.1 and 7.2 be made mutual so that our liability is subject to the same cap and exclusions as the vendor's?

findings.title: Broad indemnity covering vendor negligence with no IP indemnity
findings.quote: The Customer shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Vendor, its affiliates and their officers and employees from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses (including legal fees) arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, the Application or the Customer's business, whether or not caused by the negligence of the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: You are forced to cover all losses and legal expenses arising from the app even when they are caused by the vendor's own negligence, exposing your business to open-ended financial risk.
findings.standard: Customer indemnities should be limited to third-party claims arising from customer-provided materials, and must explicitly exclude losses resulting from the vendor's negligence or breach.
findings.suggested_ask: Can we remove the customer indemnity for vendor negligence and restrict our indemnity strictly to third-party claims arising from Customer Materials?

findings.quote: The Vendor warrants that the Application will materially conform to the SOW for sixty (60) days after acceptance of the final phase, and will correct any material non-conformity reported in that period.
findings.why_risky: Sixty days is a brief window to uncover hidden software defects, bugs, or workflow failures across 18 cafe locations and mobile operating systems.
findings.standard: A balanced software development agreement provides at least a 90-day defect warranty period post-acceptance.
findings.suggested_ask: Can we extend the defect warranty period from 60 days to 90 days following final acceptance?

missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a standard indemnity where the vendor defends and indemnifies us if the Deliverables infringe any third party's intellectual property rights.
